1.overview: A personal year 1 is the first year of a nine-year cycle, and the tradition reads it as a year of beginnings. It tends to favor planting seeds, taking initiative and deciding who you want to be next. The energy is outward and a little exposed, since new things have no track record yet.
1.work: At work and in projects, this year invites starts: a new role, a first draft, a side idea or a different way of doing the usual. You may find it easier than usual to make decisions. Pick a direction early, since what you begin now sets a tone for the next several years.
1.relationships: In relationships, you may feel a stronger pull toward independence. Friendships can shift as your interests do, and you may want more say in how time is spent. Say what you want plainly and early, and ask others what they want before the plan is set.
1.inner: Inwardly, the year may ask for courage and self-trust. You might notice impatience with old habits and a wish to prove something to yourself. Rest still matters. Starting is tiring, and a steady morning routine can hold the energy together.
1.watch: Watch for going it alone out of habit, for rushing the start and for pushing past other people's ideas. Enthusiasm can outrun planning. A few honest questions at the outset tend to save effort later.
1.reflect: What do you want to begin this year that is truly yours? Who could you invite to watch it grow, and what small first step could you take this week?

2.overview: A personal year 2 follows the burst of a 1 and tends to be quieter. The tradition reads it as a year of patience, cooperation and tending to what was planted. Progress can feel slow and subtle, and the details and the relationships around them may matter more than speed.
2.work: At work and in projects, this year suits partnerships, collaboration and careful finishing. You may find that waiting is productive: ideas ripen, and other people's input improves the plan. Pay attention to small details and to agreements, and let a slower pace work in your favor.
2.relationships: In relationships, you may be more sensitive and more attuned to others. Partnership, friendship and family can take center stage, and you may feel moods more keenly. Say what you feel in plain words. Quiet cooperation is easier when preferences are on the table.
2.inner: Inwardly, the year may ask for patience with yourself. You might notice a need for rest, gentleness and calm company. Small routines help, and so does time with people who do not need you to perform.
2.watch: Watch for people-pleasing, for over-reading other people's moods and for putting off decisions in the hope that someone else makes them. Sensitivity can tip into feeling hurt over small things. A short pause before reacting tends to help.
2.reflect: Where in your life would patience pay off more than pushing? Who would you like to listen to more closely, and what do you want that you have not yet said?

3.overview: A personal year 3 tends to bring a lighter, more social energy. The tradition reads it as a year of expression, creativity and enjoyment. Communication, play and variety may come to the front, and the question becomes what you want to say and who you want to say it with.
3.work: At work and in projects, this year suits writing, presenting, making things and sharing ideas. You may find it easier to promote yourself or to bring humor to a tense situation. Choose one or two creative aims rather than ten, and give each a finish line.
3.relationships: In relationships, you may feel more sociable and more open to fun. Invitations, new acquaintances and playful talk may be on offer. Make space for sincere conversation as well, since easy company can skate over harder subjects.
3.inner: Inwardly, the year may ask you to loosen up and trust your voice. You might notice a wish for beauty, color and laughter. Creative work in any form, even a small private one, tends to feed the whole year.
3.watch: Watch for scattering your energy, for talk that replaces action and for using charm to avoid a hard feeling. Moods can swing, and too many commitments can crowd out the real work. A simple list of priorities helps.
3.reflect: What do you most want to express this year? Who would enjoy hearing it, and what creative thing could you finish rather than only start?

4.overview: A personal year 4 tends to be a year of work and foundations. The tradition reads it as a time for organizing, building and setting up routines that last. The pace may feel steady rather than exciting, and the rewards tend to come from effort that adds up quietly.
4.work: At work and in projects, this year suits planning, systems, record keeping and finishing the unglamorous parts. You may find that careful effort now makes later years easier. Break large aims into small steps and keep to a rhythm, even when it feels slow.
4.relationships: In relationships, you may show care through reliability. Practical help, a steady presence and shared routines may count more than grand gestures. Keep room for play and spontaneity, since a year of duty can crowd out warmth.
4.inner: Inwardly, the year may ask for discipline and patience. You might notice a wish for order in your space and your time, and some frustration when things move slowly. A simple weekly review can help the effort feel visible.
4.watch: Watch for rigidity, for overwork and for treating rest as laziness. A tight plan can make small changes feel like threats. Build in slack, and notice when thoroughness has become a way of avoiding a decision.
4.reflect: What foundation would you be glad to have laid by the end of the year? Which part of your routine serves you, and which is only familiar?

5.overview: A personal year 5 sits in the middle of the cycle and tends to bring change. The tradition reads it as a year of movement, variety and freedom, when routines loosen and the unexpected is more likely to turn up. Flexibility is the skill the year seems to call for.
5.work: At work and in projects, this year suits trying new methods, traveling, networking and changing direction when something is not working. You may find that situations shift quickly. Keep a few fixed points, such as a weekly review or a deadline, so that variety does not become scatter.
5.relationships: In relationships, you may feel a stronger need for space and a taste for novelty. New people may appear, and old routines with close people may feel tight. Be clear about what you are choosing, so that others do not guess.
5.inner: Inwardly, the year may ask you to loosen your grip. You might notice restlessness and curiosity in equal measure. Movement helps, whether a walk, a trip or a new class, and so does a steady sleep schedule.
5.watch: Watch for impulsiveness, for excess and for abandoning commitments when they stop being new. The year can feel like permission to skip the dull parts. A little follow-through goes a long way toward keeping what you started.
5.reflect: What change are you ready to make on purpose, rather than waiting for it to arrive? What do you want to keep steady while everything else moves?

6.overview: A personal year 6 tends to turn attention toward home, family and responsibility. The tradition reads it as a year of care, balance and commitment, when the needs of other people and of your own surroundings come into focus. Relationships and the question of what you owe them may take center stage.
6.work: At work and in projects, this year suits teaching, service, hosting and anything that improves a shared space. You may find yourself carrying more responsibility than usual. Agree on who does what, and be clear about what is yours and what belongs to someone else.
6.relationships: In relationships, you may feel a stronger pull toward family, partners and close friends. Commitments may deepen and household questions may need attention. Ask what people need before offering what you think they should have.
6.inner: Inwardly, the year may ask you to look at balance between giving and receiving. You might notice a wish for beauty and harmony at home. Small acts of care for yourself are not selfish, and they keep the rest sustainable.
6.watch: Watch for taking on other people's load, for fussing over details and for care that expects repayment. Duty can pile up quietly. Notice when helpfulness becomes control, and let others manage their own business.
6.reflect: Who needs your care this year, and who is looking after you? What would a fair balance between giving and receiving look like in your home?

7.overview: A personal year 7 tends to turn attention inward. The tradition reads it as a year of reflection, study and rest, when the pace slows and questions about meaning become louder than questions about results. Quiet progress may matter more than visible progress.
7.work: At work and in projects, this year suits research, learning, planning and thoughtful revision. You may find that stepping back reveals what was not working. Take time to study a subject properly, and avoid forcing outcomes before the thinking is done.
7.relationships: In relationships, you may want more solitude than usual and fewer, deeper conversations. Close people may feel you drifting. Say that you need quiet and that you intend to return. A few trusted people are enough this year.
7.inner: Inwardly, the year may ask for stillness and honesty. You might notice a wish to read, write, walk alone or sort out what you actually believe. Regular quiet time, even twenty minutes, tends to be restorative.
7.watch: Watch for withdrawing too far, for over-analysis and for waiting for certainty before acting. Skepticism can slide into cynicism. Share some of what you are thinking with at least one person.
7.reflect: What question have you been circling that deserves real time? What do you understand now that you did not a year ago, and who have you told?

8.overview: A personal year 8 tends to turn attention toward effort, structure and results. The tradition reads it as a year of achievement and responsibility, when questions of authority, resources and recognition come forward. The energy is practical and driven, and the effort asked for is real.
8.work: At work and in projects, this year suits ambitious goals, leadership, negotiation and tidying up how you manage resources. You may find that effort translates into visible results more directly. Set clear targets, and be realistic about what you can sustain.
8.relationships: In relationships, you may feel the pull of your own ambitions and the demands of your schedule. Others may feel secondary if you are not careful. Schedule time with people who matter and protect it as seriously as you protect work.
8.inner: Inwardly, the year may ask you to look at your relationship with power and worth. You might notice a strong drive and some tension about whether it is enough. Rest is part of effort, not its opposite.
8.watch: Watch for overwork, for control and for measuring yourself or others by output. Pressure can harden into impatience. Notice when the goal has stopped serving what you wanted it for.
8.reflect: What would enough look like this year, in work, resources and recognition? Who decides, and what are you willing to set aside to protect what matters more?

9.overview: A personal year 9 closes the nine-year cycle. The tradition reads it as a year of completion, release and clearing out, when what has run its course comes into view. The mood tends toward compassion and a wider perspective, and toward making space for what comes next.
9.work: At work and in projects, this year suits finishing, handing over, tidying records and deciding what to carry forward. You may find that endings are clearer than usual. Close open loops properly, and avoid starting big new ventures until the cycle turns.
9.relationships: In relationships, you may feel a pull to forgive, to clear old grievances and to reassess what ties still serve you. Some connections may deepen and others may fade naturally. Be kind, be honest and let endings be plain.
9.inner: Inwardly, the year may ask for letting go. You might notice nostalgia, a wish to give things away or a sense of looking back over the whole cycle. Sorting belongings, writing things down and spending time with people you love tend to help.
9.watch: Watch for holding on to what is done, for giving until you are empty and for bitterness about what went unrecognized. Not every ending needs a ceremony. Be specific about what you are finishing.
9.reflect: What is ready to be completed or released this year? What are you carrying that no longer belongs to you, and what would you like to carry into the next cycle?
